statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL's advisory, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14681/, places this flaw in the server's GSSAPI support: after a direct TLS connection the server still accepted a GSSAPI encryption request, so a pg_hba.conf rule that requires GSSAPI encryption could be satisfied by TLS alone. It lists 17.11 as the fixed release for major version 17. The fix on the REL_17_STABLE branch, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/067a64d40f92e4e012db0367f9ff2d2ae45671ca ('Reject GSSEncRequest after direct SSL connection', tagged Security: CVE-2026-14681), changes only ProcessStartupPacket() in src/backend/tcop/backend_startup.c, and the line it changes sits inside an #ifdef ENABLE_GSS block. ENABLE_GSS is set only when PostgreSQL is configured with --with-gssapi, which is off by default; without it the server always answers a GSSAPI encryption request with N and never builds its GSSAPI transport (be-secure-gssapi.c). Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD for 3.23, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, configures without --with-gssapi and has no Kerberos build dependency, and Alpine's secfixes for the package list CVE-2026-14681 under 0, its not-affected marker (https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json; the same data also lists it under 17.11-r0). To confirm this for every published build, we unpacked all 13 postgresql17 packages (postgresql17 and its -client, -contrib, -contrib-jit, -dev, -doc, -jit, -openrc, -plperl, -plperl-contrib, -plpython3, -plpython3-contrib and -pltcl packages; no debug packages are published) for 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 on both x86_64 and aarch64, 156 packages in all, each checked against the checksum in the package index. Each build holds 123 ELF files (39 programs and 84 shared objects): 95 list the musl C library as NEEDED, 27 modules under /usr/lib/postgresql17 list no NEEDED libraries, and ltree_plpython3.so lists only libpython. None has a NEEDED entry for libgssapi_krb5, libkrb5 or any other GSSAPI or Kerberos library, and no ELF file contains the GSSAPI or Kerberos function names gss_accept_sec_context, gss_init_sec_context, gss_wrap, gss_unwrap or any krb5_ name. Each build also ships 5 static archives of PostgreSQL's own objects (libpgcommon.a, libpgcommon_shlib.a, libpgport.a, libpgport_shlib.a and libpgfeutils.a) in the -dev package, and no package contains PE, Mach-O or zip files. In every build the configure arguments recorded in the postgres server binary carry no --with-gssapi (they do carry --with-openssl), the shipped pg_config.h leaves ENABLE_GSS undefined, and the shipped PGXS Makefile.global records with_gssapi = no. The server binary contains the message 'hostgssenc record cannot match because GSSAPI is not supported by this build', which PostgreSQL compiles only when ENABLE_GSS is undefined, and lacks 'could not accept GSSAPI security context', which only the GSSAPI transport carries, while the matching TLS message 'could not accept SSL connection' is present. Without GSSAPI support the server cannot negotiate GSSAPI encryption at all, so the enforcement path the advisory describes is not in these packages.

statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14681, improper enforcement of GSSAPI encryption when a connection starts with direct TLS, so a connection can proceed over TLS alone despite pg_hba.conf rules that require GSSAPI, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are not affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14681/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14681. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
